minutes.headline: Commission ratified the highest timber bid and ordered a cease-and-desist on any further clearing at 238 Fire Road 16.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission handled a continued notice of intent, ratified the forester's choice of the highest timber harvest bid for two town properties, and took up enforcement matters including 238 Fire Road 16 and a driveway encroachment at 192 Townsend Harbor Road. The agent announced his retirement and a liaison seat on the open space committee is vacant. The meeting adjourned to April 6.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none was offered.
Resident of 192 Townsend Harbor Road updated the commission on removing the driveway section on conservation land and moving it; a contractor plan is expected in a couple of weeks.
An abutter (Leah) reported that cutting or clearing at 238 Fire Road 16 appeared ongoing, and earlier raised a conifer mix for replanting.
A property owner (Nick) asked about trees on his plan that were listed inaccurately and offered a site walk.

votes.motion: Continue the notice of intent for 445 Townsend Harbor Road (railroad tie steps/retaining wall) to April 6, pending a DEP number.
Ratify the forester's decision to award the timber harvest to the highest bidder.
Initiate a cease and desist at 238 Fire Road 16 if clearing is outside the specified bounds.
Adjourn, with the next meeting by Zoom on April 6.

budget_items.topic: Timber harvest bids, Hollis Road and Northfield Road
budget_items.what_was_said: Three bids were received; the forester recommends the highest, from King Farms. The bidders pay the town for the wood, with a deposit on signing.
The forester proposed a deposit hold with full payments once harvest can begin after the ground dries. The payment flows to the town, not from it.
The fee for a request for determination of applicability was stated as payable to the town.

decisions.decision: 192 Townsend Harbor Road owner to have his contractor contact the agent and file an RDA for the driveway work rather than proceed by town counsel enforcement.
Site walk for 441 Townsend Harbor Road tentatively set for Saturday, April 2, with an updated plan to be submitted first.
Open space committee liaison seat left vacant until absent members can be informed.
Agent to report back April 6 on 615 Townsend Street, with the building inspector leading enforcement.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to ratify the forester's decision to award the timber harvest for two town properties to the highest bidder.
The commission voted to start a cease and desist at 238 Fire Road 16 if clearing is found outside the specified bounds.
The commission continued the notice of intent for 445 Townsend Harbor Road to April 6, pending a DEP number.
The owner of 192 Townsend Harbor Road is to have a contractor contact the agent and file an RDA for driveway work on conservation land.
The open space committee liaison seat was left vacant, and a site walk for 441 Townsend Harbor Road was tentatively set for April 2.

why_it_matters: The timber sale pays money to the town rather than costing it, so the winning bid is revenue from town-owned land.
The Fire Road 16 order and the Townsend Harbor Road driveway matter to abutters and to anyone affected by work on or next to protected conservation land.
watch_next: The commission adjourned to April 6, when the 445 Townsend Harbor Road notice of intent returns and the agent reports on 615 Townsend Street.
A contractor plan for the 192 Townsend Harbor Road driveway is expected in a couple of weeks, followed by an RDA filing.
